Commentary.Commentary: New Zealand need a good start here if they have any hopes of reaching this target.
We are back for the runchase. Chad Bowes and Tom Latham will open the inning for New Zealand. Shaheen Afridi has the new ball and will begin proceedings. Let's go...

For the Kiwis, Matt Henry was the standout bowler as he managed to pick up a couple of wickets giving away just 29 runs. He was well helped by James Neesham and Rachin Ravindra who scaled a wicket each. The target is not a big one, but looking at what happened in the 1st T20 international New Zealand would be looking to put up a fight in this game and level the series by chasing this down.

It is all about Babar Azam at the moment as the everyone looks to be still celebrating his outstanding knock! We are at the halfway stage of this game as Pakistan has posted a total of 192 runs in their quota of 20 overs. After being asked to bat, Pakistan started off well with the opening stand of 99 runs before Mohammad Rizwan eventually got out after notching up his half-century. There was a cluster of wickets in the middle stage but Iftikhar Ahmed and Babar Azam batted brilliantly and managed to post a total that the bowlers can fight for and defend. Babar Azam batted to the very end and scored 17 runs in the last over to reach the landmark.

Babar Azam goes really hard at the ball and creams this to deep cover for a one-bounce four. Babar Azam thumps his chest and jumps in the air as his teammates join him in celebration.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tom Latham(C/WK), Chad Bowes, Will Young, Daryl Mitchell, Mark Chapman, James Neesham, Rachin Ravindra (In place of Ish Sodhi), Cole McConchie (In place of Adam Milne), Henry Shipley, Matt Henry, Benjamin Lister.
Pakistan (Playing XI) - Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Babar Azam (C), Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub, Shadab Khan, Iftikhar Ahmed, Imad Wasim, Faheem Ashraf, Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf, Zaman Khan.
TOSS - The captains are out in the middle. The coin is flipped into the air and lands in favor of Pakistan. They have elected to BAT first.

New Zealand on the contrary had a day to forget as they were poor in all three departments of the game. The bowlers were able to bowl out the hosts but the batters couldn't back it up and were bundled out on 94. Mark Chapman was the only one who showed some resilience and fought for the side but was not backed up by anyone. The Kiwis would be heavily relying upon the top order to fire if they are to have a better time in this outing. Will they be able to overcome their disappointment and get their first win on this long tour? Or will Pakistan continue their dominance? We will find out soon. Stay tuned for the toss and team updates.

Pakistan won the first game convincingly despite being in a situation of bother at one point in time when they were batting. They still managed to post a solid total on the board and their bowling was spot on as they did not let the visitors get to the three-figure mark. Haris Rauf was outstanding with the ball and the same would be expected of him in the second game as well. Young sensation Saim Ayub was brilliant with the bat along with the experienced head of Fakhar Zaman though the team would be looking for a better display from ace batter Babar Azam.

Hello, and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen to our coverage of the second match in the five-match T20I series as Pakistan take on New Zealand at Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore. The hosts have a 1-0 lead in this long series and will want to take an early advantage by maintaining their winning momentum. The Kiwis will want the forget their last match in a hurry and have an opportunity to reverse their fortune by leveling the series in this quick turnaround.
... MATCH DAY ...

It is time for the second T20I of the New Zealand tour of Pakistan. The first game was dominated by the hosts as they won it comprehensively with a margin of 88 runs. The hosts scored a good total as Fakhar Zaman and Saim Ayub put up a good show. Pakistan though went on a bit of a rollercoaster ride after Ayub’s wicket. The men in green kept losing wickets at regular intervals but they also assured the run rate kept growing. They will look to have a steady start and restrict their loss of wickets in their next game. On the bowling front, Haris Rauf was quick to wrap up the tail and bagged her career-best T20I figures of 4/18. They will be pleased with their performance and will look to put up a better show in front of their home crowd. For the visitors, it was just a bad day. They were off to a shaky start inside the Powerplay. None of their batters performed well and they will look to bounce back. The hosts have started the series on an assertive note and they will look to take a 2-0 lead in the series. Can they do it? Or will the Kiwis bounce back and level the series? Let's find out together.
